label: Unmanned systems operator
description: An organization that flies unmanned aircraft or systems (a university UAS lab, a public-safety drone unit, an inspection contractor): flight operations and test sites, ground control stations, C2/telemetry links, GNSS/RTK, payloads, research data pipelines, batteries, hangars and labs, and the airspace authorizations (Part 107, LAANC, COA, a nearby Class C airport) they fly under.

vocabulary.facility: the flight operations program (flight test sites, hangars, labs and ground control stations)
vocabulary.public: the campus or community under the flight areas, nearby pilots and sponsors
vocabulary.frontline: remote pilots in command, visual observers, GCS operators, payload engineers, the airworthiness lead, the safety officer
vocabulary.operationsCenter: the flight operations center / mission control room

it: research data pipeline and storage (flight logs, imagery)
campus or corporate email and identity
the vendor cloud (telemetry and imagery sync)
ot: UAS detection systems (RF, radar, Remote ID receivers)

roles.name: Director of Flight Operations (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Owns the aircraft, the crews, the flight schedule and the go/no-go.

roles.name: Systems & Cybersecurity Lead (Technical Lead)
roles.description: Owns the GCS, links, data pipeline and the investigation.

roles.name: Aviation Safety Officer
roles.description: Owns the safety case, the airspace authorizations and regulator reporting.

roles.name: Communications Lead (PIO)
roles.description: Owns sponsor, campus and press messaging.

roles.name: Security / Campus Safety Liaison
roles.description: Owns the hangar, the test site perimeter and the law-enforcement liaison.

roles.name: Chief Remote Pilot
roles.description: Owns crew qualification, mission go/no-go and the lost-link procedure.

roles.name: Maintenance / Airworthiness Lead
roles.description: Owns inspections, parts traceability and return to service after an anomaly.

roles.name: Risk Manager / General Counsel
roles.description: Owns insurance notice, privacy complaints and the legal limits on detection and mitigation.

outsideParties: the FAA (Flight Standards, the local FSDO, the nearby Class C tower; 107.9 safety event reports within 10 days)
the FCC (spectrum, equipment authorization, the Covered List)
local law enforcement and campus safety
the university or corporate export-control office
neighboring landowners under the flight areas
DHS Program Executive Office for Drones and C-UAS
the FBI National Counter-UAS Training Center
a certified state or local counter-UAS law-enforcement team (SAFER SKIES Act authority, in effect since 1 Jul 2026)
mediaChannels: a neighbor's post about a drone over their yard
a student post on Instagram from the flight line
the student newspaper or a trade outlet

sceneAnchors.public: at an open grass flight test field: a multirotor drone on a landing pad, a crew in high-visibility vests at a folding table, orange cones, a windsock, clear sky
sceneAnchors.control: inside a ground control station trailer: an operator at a laptop console with a dark screen, telemetry radios and antennas on the roof, cables, dim light
sceneAnchors.exterior: inside a small hangar: several drones on benches, battery chargers on a rack, a fixed-wing airframe on a stand, roll-up door open to daylight

noiseExamples: a battery charger showing a cell-balance warning
a student asking for a hangar key card
a mower blocking the taxi path to the pad
a sponsor asking for a logo on the airframe
pressureExamples: a neighbor posting a photo of a drone over their backyard
the Class C tower calling about an unidentified track
the sponsor's program manager asking whether research data leaked
the student newspaper asking about a crash
the FAA FSDO asking for the flight logs
the 10-day FAA 107.9 report deadline after a flyaway that damaged a car
a rogue drone over the test site with police asking whether to call in a certified counter-UAS team
